The interactive Shiny explorer

Source: vignettes/articles/shiny-app.Rmd
shiny-app.Rmd

run_dietview() launches an interactive Shiny app over a prepared dataset. It is the fastest way to explore a diet before committing to a static dashboard. (Chunks here are shown but not run — the app needs shiny and, for the table, DT.)

install.packages(c("shiny", "DT"))
library(DietView)

dat <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "dietview_example.csv", package = "DietView"),
                na.strings = c("NA", ""))
lin <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "dietview_example_lineage.csv", package = "DietView"),
                na.strings = c("NA", ""))
spec <- dv_spec(predator = "predator_species_common_name", stomach = "stomach_id",
                prey_id = "aphia_id", prey_name = "verified_name",
                weight = "prey_weight", digestion = "digestion_level_id",
                covariates = c("period", "size_class", "size_bin", "region"))
prep <- dv_prepare(dat, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = lin)

run_dietview(prep)

What the app offers

  • a predator selector;
  • a mode switch (count / occurrence / weight);
  • an optional facet covariate to compare levels side by side;
  • a rank selector for the importance table.

The server subsets the records for the chosen predator, builds the tree reactively with dv_build_tree(), renders the sunburst with the shared palette, and shows the within-rank importance table for the chosen rank.

When to use the app vs. the dashboard

Use the app for live exploration on your own machine. Use dv_build_html() / dv_deploy() to produce a self-contained HTML file you can archive, email, or serve — no R session required by the reader.
